purpose: Machine-readable contract for UCI overlay authority resolution (Layer B). Implemented by shell/apps/openclash-guard/uci-overlay-resolve.sh and asserted by tests/test_openclash_guard_uci_overlay_resolve.py. Scope discipline: compute effective values ONLY where an authoritative source defines the gate; everything else is an explicit contract gap (deferred), never invented.

trustModel.policy: UCI is operator intent, never a second policy authority. Computed effective values constrain the operator request by signed policy (ceiling/floor) and live capability; UCI can only NARROW, never widen.
trustModel.rawVsEffective: The snapshot keeps operator intent (raw) distinct from the resolved value (effective). Diagnostics report both so drift is explainable.
trustModel.resolveGate: guard_uci_overlay_resolve() REQUIRES a loaded AND valid Layer-A snapshot. On an invalid or unloaded snapshot it returns non-zero and presents NO effective state as usable.
trustModel.authorityInputs: Provenance vs schema: (1) PROVENANCE — production resolution consumes a runtime policy ONLY after the authoritative guard_policy_load() validation (and the signed-runtime release chain establishing its origin) has succeeded. This module does not authenticate provenance and never duplicates cryptographic/signature logic. (2) SCHEMA SANITY — the resolver ALSO runs a focused surface check (defense-in-depth) on the policy it reads: present, well-formed JSON, supported schemaVersion (1), services + protectionClasses, every service referencing an existing class, directAllowed and firewallKillSwitch boolean. This check must NOT be described as establishing an authenticated policy. A missing/malformed/unsupported-schema policy fails the schema gate (refuse rc 3, resolved state stays 0, no permissive default such as an empty-services-list hiding the fail-closed floor). The live DNS observation must be a real observed value (adguardhome|dnsmasq|none); empty/unset/unexpected is NOT the observed 'none' and also refuses. Diagnostics reports authorityInputs availability without mutating resolved state.
trustModel.snapshotCoherence: Layer-A collection is snapshot-coherent, not atomic. `uci show` is used ONLY as a coherence FINGERPRINT (captured before and after, with explicit exit-status checks — never `|| true`, so two failed captures can never compare equal-and-succeed). Semantic VALUES are read with the real `uci get` CLI (scalar) and `uci -d <newline> get` (IPv4 list) so the UCI CLI itself decodes upstream quoting/escaping; there is no home-grown shell quote parser and no `eval` of `uci show`. A failed semantic field read discards the candidate. Fingerprint before/after comparison provides before/after DRIFT DETECTION with a bounded retry (GUARD_UCI_OVERLAY_MAX_ATTEMPTS, default 2); a persistent change or read failure yields a non-zero load and no defaults-as-content snapshot is published. Residual guarantee: drift detection + bounded retry + the classic ABA limitation (a value that changes A->B->A within the window is not detected); NOT a UCI transaction.
trustModel.resolutionCommitAtomicity: The internal commit is atomic. guard_uci_overlay_invalidate_resolved_state() runs first; only if _guard_uci_overlay_resolve_apply() succeeds is _GUARD_UCO_RESOLVED set to 1, otherwise state is invalidated again and resolution returns non-zero. A partial computation can never leave partial effective globals behind or accidentally mark the state resolved. This uses explicit handling, not set -e reliance inside shell functions.
trustModel.resolvedStateLifecycle: Layer-B maintains an explicit resolved-state flag (_GUARD_UCO_RESOLVED, default 0). Every overlay re-load invalidates all resolved state (_GUARD_UCO_EFFECTIVE_* and notes cleared, flag -> 0) BEFORE a new snapshot is observable, so a stale effective value can never leak across snapshots. The flag becomes 1 only after the complete normal resolution path succeeds. guard_uci_overlay_resolve_state_valid() means loaded AND layer-A-valid AND layer-B-resolution-completed (NOT merely loaded+valid), and goes false again after any re-load until re-resolved. guard_uci_overlay_effective() for a resolved gated option REFUSES (non-zero) when no completed resolution exists for the current snapshot; it never falls back to the normalized UCI value. guard_uci_overlay_resolve_diagnostics() is read-only: inference runs in a subshell so it cannot mutate _GUARD_UCO_RESOLVED, _GUARD_UCO_EFFECTIVE_*, or notes in the caller.

signed-policy-gated-route-mode.rule: A requested 'direct' is honoured only when the service's protection class has directAllowed=true; otherwise effective falls back to 'proxy'. Region constraints are NOT part of this config-time gate (allowedRegions constrains live route evaluation in guard_policy_region_allowed, not the snapshot).

signed-policy-floor.rule: If any service protection class has firewallKillSwitch=true OR directAllowed=false (mirrors guard_policy_needs_failclosed), fail-closed is a signed REQUIREMENT: an operator dns.fail_closed=0 cannot lower the floor and effective stays 1. Otherwise the operator value is honoured.

live-capability-gated-backend.rule: Mirrors guard_dns_backend() detection (adguardhome | dnsmasq | none). 'auto' resolves to the detected backend else 'none'; an explicit request is honoured only when it equals the detected backend, else effective is 'none' (a preference cannot install capability). Downstream consumers key off this EFFECTIVE backend, not the raw live input.

gaps.note: These options are contract-marked (signed-policy-gated / live-capability-gated) but their exact Layer-B resolution semantics are NOT defined by any authoritative contract today. They are surfaced as DEFERRED (normalized passthrough, explicitly flagged) and MUST NOT be consumed as an authoritative effective value until a contract update lands. Unresolved semantics are intentionally preferred over invented semantics.

deferred.reason: No authoritative contract defines resolver-sync capability. Current runtime behavior is NOT a simple 'backend is capable' flag: guard_dns_domain_set_backend maps dnsmasq->dnsmasq-nftset, and adguardhome only promotes via the separate guard_resolver_sync_backend capability verification. Treating adguardhome/dnsmasq as generically sync-capable would invent semantics.

redaction: Resolution reasons name the constraint that fired (e.g. 'direct not permitted by signed policy', 'requested DNS backend not detected live') and never echo URLs, tokens, or credentials.
